title: Thy Favours Lord, Surprise Our Souls
description: Thy Favours Lord, Surprise Our Souls in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 45, headed “God's condescension to our worship”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy fa-vours Lord, sur-prise our souls; Will the E-ter-nal dwell with us? What canst thou find be-neath the poles To tempt thy char-iot down-ward thus?

lines: Thy favours Lord, surprise our souls;
Will the Eternal dwell with us?
What canst thou find beneath the poles
To tempt thy chariot downward thus?
Still might he fill his starry throne,
And please his ears with Gabriel's songs;
But th' heavenly Majesty comes down,
And bows to hearken to our tongues.
Great God, what poor returns we pay
For love so infinite as thine!
Words are but air, and tongues but clay,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
